paragraphs: Friend, this passage is about proof. Jesus was really dead. The soldiers checked, and when they came to Jesus and saw that He was already dead, they did not break His legs (John 19:33). Then the writer, who saw it, stops and tells us why he is telling it: "so that you also may believe" (John 19:35).

Here's the part that gets me. Scripture said it ahead of time: "Not one of His bones will be broken" (John 19:36), and "They will look on the One they have pierced" (John 19:37). Soldiers, a spear and a rush to beat a Sabbath, and God's Word still came true down to the bones. If His Word held up in a moment that dark, you can trust it in yours. That's why I keep my ovens ready, friend.

Then look at who steps up. Joseph of Arimathea had kept his faith secret for fear of the Jews, and he walked straight to Pilate and asked for the body (John 19:38). Nicodemus, who first came to Jesus at night, showed up with about seventy-five pounds of spices (John 19:39). I think that's what a hidden faith looks like when it finally comes out into the light. Your faith doesn't have to be loud or perfect to get brave, baker, and the story isn't over yet.
